- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > true by >3%), model overcorrects; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% after sentiment drop.
- Model often underestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is weak; add 1–3% bias to first 5–7 days if sentiment <0.5.
- If true price deviates >5% from forecast for 3+ consecutive days, apply “mean reversion correction” — adjust forecast toward historical 14-day average.
- Forecasting near sentiment extremes (0.00 or 1.00) shows high volatility bias — use 1.5x smoothing factor for sentiment-driven corrections.
